core_obligations: Reduce to A local with maximal ideal p, write N = S^{-1}N' for a finitely presented B-module N' by clearing denominators, and use Noetherianity of B/mB to conclude that the kernel K of N'/mN' -> N/mN is finitely generated (proof lines 7277-7283).
Choose s in S annihilating K and replace B by B_s, so that the elements of S act injectively on N'/mN' (proof lines 7283-7286).

Descend to a finitely generated model: choose A_0 in A essentially of finite type over Z, a finite type map A_0 -> B_0 with B = A tensor_{A_0} B_0 and a finite B_0-module N'_0 with N' = A tensor_{A_0} N'_0, and verify that I = m_{A_0}A works, because N'/IN' = N'_0/m_{A_0}N'_0 tensor_{k_{A_0}} A/I is free over A/I and multiplication by S remains injective modulo the maximal ideal (proof lines 7287-7299).
proof_roadmap: Localise and clear denominators, then kill the finite kernel to make S act injectively modulo the maximal ideal (proof lines 7277-7286).
Build a finite model over a subring of A essentially of finite type over Z (proof lines 7287-7291).
Verify freeness after dividing by I and conclude universal injectivity, hence the pure spreadout (proof lines 7292-7299).
difficulty_reason: In the situation of the reference equation, the lemma asserts that for every prime p of A there is a finitely generated ideal I inside pA_p such that over A_p/I the module in question has a pure spreadout (statement lines 7269-7274). The proof first replaces A by its localisation at p, then clears denominators to write N = S^{-1}N' for a finitely presented B-module N', uses that B/mB is Noetherian so that the kernel K of N'/mN' -> N/mN is finitely generated, and picks s in S annihilating K so that, after replacing B by B_s, the elements of S act injectively on N'/mN' (proof lines 7277-7286). The second half is a descent of finite presentation: one chooses a local subring A_0 of A essentially of finite type over Z, a finite type ring map A_0 -> B_0 with B = A tensor_{A_0} B_0, and a finite B_0-module N'_0 with N' = A tensor_{A_0} N'_0, and claims that I = m_{A_0} A works; indeed N'/IN' = N'_0/m_{A_0}N'_0 tensor_{k_{A_0}} A/I is free over A/I, and multiplication by elements of S stays injective after dividing out by the maximal ideal, which gives universal injectivity of N'/IN' -> N/IN (proof lines 7287-7299). Building the finite model over a subring of finite type and recognising that freeness plus one injectivity statement yields the pure spreadout is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.
